previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and respiratory failure following a drug overdose involving benzodiazepines, opiates, and cocaine. He was intubated for airway protection and managed in the ICU with supportive care, including IV hydralazine for hypertension and antibiotics for suspected UTI. Toxicology and psychiatry consultations indicated a non-suicidal mixed ingestion. He was successfully extubated on hospital day two, completed a course of antibiotics, and stabilized medically. His chronic conditions, including CKD, neurogenic bladder, and seizure disorder, were managed without complication. He was discharged home with simplified medications, a short course of oral nitrofurantoin, and referrals for psychiatry, substance use counseling, and primary care follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ with T12 paraplegia, multiple right lower extremity
fractures.  Please evaluate for deep vein thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  No prior studies available for comparison.

FINDINGS:  Exam is severely limited due to patient's paraplegia, contracted
left lower extremity and multiple right lower extremity fractures and
overlying splint.

In the left lower extremity, the common femoral and proximal superficial
femoral veins were the only vessels able to be evaluated and they demonstrate
normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation.

In the right lower extremity, the right common femoral, superficial femoral,
and popliteal veins were assessed and demonstrate normal compressibility, flow
and augmentation throughout.

IMPRESSION:  Limited exam.  No deep vein thrombosis identified in the left
common femoral and proximal superficial femoral veins nor in the right common
femoral through popliteal veins.

INDICATION:  Preoperative evaluation.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to chest radiograph performed ___.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral radiograph demonstrates unremarkable mediastinal,
hilar and cardiac contours.  Low lung volumes are noted bilaterally with
resultant crowding of the vasculature structures.  No overt pulmonary edema
evident.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax evident.  Thoracic vertebral
stabilization devices are again noted.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.

INDICATION:  Fracture status post reduction and realignment.  Please evaluate.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to tib-fib radiographs performed ___.

FINDINGS:  Redemonstration of the minimally displaced obliquely oriented
fracture through the proximal aspect of the tibia and fibula with slight
improved alignment.  Small joint effusion noted.  Significant soft tissue
swelling is present overlying knee and fracture site.

IMPRESSION:  Slightly improved alignment of the minimally displaced fracture
of the proximal tibia and fibula. Small joint effusion.

HISTORY:  Status post fall with right intertrochanteric and tibiofibular
fracture.  Evaluate for pelvic or hip fracture.  The patient is paraplegic;
status post fall.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___, right tibia-fibula
___ and right femur and right knee ___.

TECHNIQUE:  AP pelvis, single view.

FINDINGS:  There is similar dislocation of the left femoral head superiorly
and posteriorly in relation to the acetabulum.  Severe degenerative changes
are seen in bilateral hip joints.  The known right  greater trochanteric
fracture is less apparent on current view.  Lucency with sclerosis in the left
iliac wing is similar, likely bone donor site.  Partially imaged hardware is
seen at the lower lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Similar dislocation of the left femoral head superior and posterior in
relation to the acetabulum.
2.  Right greater trochanteric fracture.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Right proximal tibia fracture in cast.

RIGHT TIBIA AND FIBULA, FOUR FILMS.

Following casting the alignment of the fractured tibia and fibula is unchanged
since the prior films and appears satisfactory.  Alignment of ankle appears
normal.

HISTORY:  Fracture postop casting.

AP view of the femur plus lateral of distal femur.  No lateral or the proximal
femur was obtained.  

Detail is considerably obscured by the overlying cast. There is a fracture of
the proximal tibia, with slight lateral displacement of the distal fragment
and lateral apex angulation.  Possible proximal fibular fracture.    There
does appear to be a knee joint effusion, with fat-fluid level. There is
irregularity of the greater trochanter of the proximal femur and patchy
density in this area, as well, of uncertain significance.  There is background
diffuse osteopenia, much greater than expected in someone of this age.
